text:
ada: Heads up - onboarding report: Windows new hire hit auth break in sampleapp after rotating creds. They swapped REDWOOD_API_KEY but we only had REDWOOD_PROJECT_NAME in their env, sampleapp expects REDWOOD_PROJECT.
mike: What was the SDK error?
ada: `401 Unauthorized: invalid key scope` (no extra hint). Only reproducible when REDWOOD_PROJECT is unset.
olivia: We have inconsistent env names across tooling: Go + Python read REDWOOD_PROJECT, Node uses REDWOOD_PROJECT_NAME, CLI supports --project. Also sampleapp README mentions REDWOOD_ORG but not project scoping.
trent: Oof. That mismatch will silently fail during key rotation. If the new key is project-scoped and the app reads the wrong var, it looks like the key is bad.
mike: Two quick fixes: 1) SDK parity: all SDKs should accept both env vars for now, preferring REDWOOD_PROJECT. 2) Add a startup validation in sampleapp that fails fast with a friendly message if an API key is present but project scope missing.
olivia: Also retry logic: CI rotates short-lived tokens and we've seen SDKs retry on 401 indefinitely. Need to treat 401/403 as non-retry unless response includes `Retry-After` or `x-redwood-retryable-auth: true`.
ada: Proposed auth semantics to standardize across SDKs: - Determine project via env precedence: REDWOOD_PROJECT -> REDWOOD_PROJECT_NAME -> CLI flag. - If request returns 401/403: if header `Retry-After` present, backoff+retry; else raise AuthError with hint: "check REDWOOD_PROJECT env var or pass --project" and don't retry.
trent: Can we log a correlating header from server like `x-redwood-expected-scope: project` when the server rejects due to scope mismatch? That would make troubleshooting trivial.
mike: Good call. I'll follow up with backend to add that header.
olivia: Ops ask: add a CI smoke test in onboarding pipeline that runs sampleapp with only REDWOOD_API_KEY set (no project env) to catch this early.
ada: I'll update sampleapp README and onboarding doc now: explicitly list env vars, show precedence, and include the troubleshooting snippet: `if 401 and x-redwood-expected-scope: project -> export REDWOOD_PROJECT=...`
trent: I'll open parity PRs for Node/Java to fallback to REDWOOD_PROJECT and add unit tests simulating env permutations. Assigning to @trent.
ci-bot: CI: node-sdk-auth-fallbacks #789 queued
mike: Also add small integration test in SDKs asserting that auth 401 without Retry-After does not trigger retry loop.
olivia: Timeline: README + onboarding doc patch today; SDK parity + tests in next patch release (few hours). Backend header is a separate ticket.
ada: Thanks. Follow-ups: trent PR, mike test, ops CI smoke job. Tagging devex and eng-runtime for visibility.
